questions.q: What real DBA job does the Test-BackupAge script automate?
options: Checking that every database on every server has a recent backup, flagging anything overdue or never backed up
Creating new databases automatically on a schedule
Automatically resizing storage accounts in Azure
Installing SQL Server updates without manual approval
questions.explain: The script's whole purpose is catching missing or stale backups before they become a real incident.

questions.q: Where does Test-BackupAge get its backup history data from?
options: Invoke-DbaQuery running T-SQL against msdb.dbo.backupset
A manually maintained spreadsheet the script reads
Azure Cloud Shell's built-in backup tracker
It estimates backup age without querying anything
questions.explain: msdb.dbo.backupset is the real SQL Server system table for backup history, queried via dbatools' Invoke-DbaQuery.

questions.q: What is the difference between the script's inner and outer foreach loops?
options: The inner loop walks each database's query result inside the function; the outer loop walks the whole server list, calling the function once per server
They do exactly the same thing and one is redundant
The inner loop only runs if the outer loop fails
The outer loop iterates over columns, not servers
questions.explain: The function operates per-server internally, and the outer loop applies that function across the full server list.

questions.q: What would happen if -MaxHoursOld were never passed in when calling Test-BackupAge?
options: The function would use its default value of 24
The script would immediately throw an error and stop
It would default to 0 hours, flagging every database as overdue
The parameter is required and the function cannot run without it
questions.explain: [int]$MaxHoursOld = 24 in the param block supplies a default when the caller doesn't override it, as covered in Lesson 13.

questions.q: Why does the lesson call this script realistic rather than a toy example?
options: It's something a DBA would actually run, likely as a scheduled task, and is intentionally incomplete in a realistic way (no alert yet, console output only)
It has no practical use and exists only to demonstrate syntax
It is a complete, production-ready product with nothing left to add
It only works in a lab environment and could never run against real servers
questions.explain: The lesson frames it as genuinely useful but purposely still needing extension — exactly the situation Lesson 18 addresses.
